edges.description: Supersaturated bile is metastable, so the dissolved cholesterol can undergo a phase transition once nucleation is accelerated.

edges.description: Crystals nucleated within the mucin gel are the solid phase that subsequently aggregates and coalesces into macroscopic stones.
Retained crystals in a stagnant, mucin-rich lumen aggregate and grow.
Only a minority of stones ever impact; what determines which do is not established, which is why this edge is not direct.
Cystic-duct obstruction by an impacted stone produces the episodic visceral pain that defines symptomatic disease.
Sustained obstruction with raised intraluminal pressure produces acute inflammation of the gallbladder wall.
A stone passing into the common bile duct obstructs biliary drainage.
A stone impacted at the ampulla obstructs the pancreatic duct.
Insulin resistance raises biliary cholesterol secretion, but the intermediate steps between adiposity and the measured saturation index are not established in these sources.

nodes.description: Episodic severe right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, typically postprandial and lasting hours, caused by a stone obstructing the cystic duct. This is the presentation that defines symptomatic gallstone disease and the indication for cholecystectomy.

evidence.snippet: Gallstones may present as biliary pain, acute cholecystitis, biliary obstruction or pancreatitis
Cholecystectomy is indicated for patients with symptomatic gallstones or sludge.

nodes.description: Acute inflammation of the gallbladder wall following sustained cystic-duct obstruction, and the complication that converts elective surgery into an urgent indication.

evidence.snippet: Acute cholecystitis is an indication for early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 24 hours of admission to hospital.

nodes.description: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography to clear stones from the common bile duct, done before cholecystectomy when the duct is involved. Endosonography first reduces the number of purely diagnostic procedures.

evidence.snippet: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography should only be carried out as part of a planned therapeutic intervention; endosonography beforehand lessens the number of endoscopic retrograde cholangiographies that need to be performed.

nodes.description: Gallbladder smooth muscle contracts incompletely after a meal, leaving an enlarged residual volume and stagnant bile. The prolonged residence time is what converts nucleation into stone formation: crystals that would otherwise be emptied into the intestine are retained long enough to aggregate and grow. The cited review lists it as one of three conditions of which one or more must be present, so it is modelled as an independent input to stone growth rather than as a consequence of nucleation.

evidence.snippet: Cholesterol crystal formation requires the presence of one or more of the following: (a) cholesterol supersaturation, (b) accelerated nucleation, or (c) gallbladder hypomotility/bile stasis.

nodes.description: Cholesterol monohydrate crystals, embedded in the mucin gel of a poorly emptying gallbladder, aggregate and coalesce into macroscopic stones. Growth is sustained while supersaturation and stasis persist, which is why stones are usually multiple and why they recur after non-operative clearance.

evidence.snippet: Hypersecretion of gallbladder mucus occurs in response to a lithogenic diet in experimental animals, and mucus accumulates as a viscous gel within the gallbladder lumen before gallstone formation.

nodes.description: Acute pancreatitis caused by a stone obstructing the pancreatic duct at the ampulla, the most dangerous common complication of gallstones.

evidence.snippet: Gallstones may present as biliary pain, acute cholecystitis, biliary obstruction or pancreatitis, but it is not clear who will develop symptoms

nodes.description: Hepatocytes secrete cholesterol into bile in excess of the bile salts and phospholipids needed to hold it in mixed micelles and vesicles, so gallbladder bile becomes supersaturated and physically metastable. The excess is driven by the hepatocanalicular sterol transporter ABCG5/G8 in the genetic form and by insulin resistance and obesity in the common metabolic form. This is the step that distinguishes cholesterol stones from pigment stones, which instead precipitate bilirubin and arise in chronic haemolysis, cirrhosis or biliary infection.

evidence.snippet: Cholesterol crystal formation requires the presence of one or more of the following: (a) cholesterol supersaturation, (b) accelerated nucleation, or (c) gallbladder hypomotility/bile stasis.

Generally, pigment stones are formed by the precipitation of bilirubin in bile, with black stones associated with chronic hemolytic states, cirrhosis, Gilbert syndrome, or cystic fibrosis, and brown stones associated with chronic bacterial or parasitic infections.

evidence.reference_title: Increased gallstone risk in humans conferred by common variant of hepatic ATP-binding cassette transporter for cholesterol.
evidence.snippet: The linkage and association studies identified the cholesterol transporter ABCG5/G8 as a genetic determinant of gallstone formation, or LITH gene, in humans.

nodes.description: Removal of the gallbladder, which eliminates both the stones and the organ in which they form, and is therefore definitive rather than suppressive. Indicated for symptomatic stones, and performed early when acute cholecystitis has supervened.

evidence.snippet: The timing of treatment for gallstone disease is an essential determinant of therapeutic success.
Cholecystectomy can be performed in any trimester of pregnancy, if urgently indicated.

nodes.description: Gallbladder epithelium hypersecretes mucin, which accumulates as a viscous gel in the gallbladder lumen before any stone is visible. Hydrophobic domains on the mucin protein core bind the cholesterol-enriched vesicles carried in supersaturated bile and accelerate nucleation of solid cholesterol monohydrate crystals, which first appear inside that gel.

evidence.reference_title: Gallbladder mucin as a pronucleating agent for cholesterol monohydrate crystals in bile.
evidence.snippet: In both animals and man, the initial stage of cholesterol gallstone formation, the nucleation of cholesterol monohydrate crystals, occurs within the mucus gel.

evidence.reference_title: Gallbladder mucin as a pronucleating agent for cholesterol monohydrate crystals in bile.
evidence.snippet: Binding of cholesterol-enriched vesicles to hydrophobic domains on the mucin protein core appears to be critical for the acceleration of cholesterol crystal nucleation by mucin.

evidence.reference_title: Gallbladder mucin as a pronucleating agent for cholesterol monohydrate crystals in bile.
evidence.snippet: Inhibition of mucus secretion with aspirin prevents gallstone formation in the cholesterol-fed prairie dog, indicating the importance of mucus in gallstone formation.

nodes.description: Metabolic risk acts on the supersaturation step and is the main reason population prevalence is rising. Central adiposity and diabetes are associated with gallstones, and diabetes with larger stones.

evidence.reference_title: Management of gallstones and its related complications.
evidence.snippet: For cholesterol gallstone disease, moreover, a strong link exists between this disease and highly prevalent metabolic disorders such as obesity, dyslipidemia, type 2 diabetes, hyperinsulinemia, hypertriglyceridemia and the metabolic syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and risk factors for gallstone disease: A population-based cross-sectional study.
evidence.snippet: Diabetes (OR 4.144, 95% CI 1.171-14.671, P = 0.028) was a risk factor for the formation of gallstones with diameters >=1 cm

nodes.description: Jaundice from obstruction of the common bile duct by a migrated stone, which requires endoscopic duct clearance before the gallbladder is removed.

evidence.snippet: Gallstones may present as biliary pain, acute cholecystitis, biliary obstruction or pancreatitis
After successful endoscopic clearance of the biliary pathway, patients who also have cholelithiasis should undergo laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours.

nodes.description: A stone impacted in the gallbladder neck or cystic duct raises intraluminal pressure and produces biliary pain and, when obstruction persists, acute cholecystitis. A stone that passes into the common bile duct obstructs biliary drainage, giving jaundice, and can obstruct the pancreatic duct, giving gallstone pancreatitis. Most stones never reach this node: the majority of people with incidentally detected gallstones remain asymptomatic.

evidence.snippet: Gallstones may present as biliary pain, acute cholecystitis, biliary obstruction or pancreatitis, but it is not clear who will develop symptoms and what are the commonest initial symptoms.
Studies of the natural history of silent gallstones suggest that a large majority of patients with such stones will remain asymptomatic.
